 Tennis-Svitolina stuns Sabalenka to reach WTA Finals semis
 By Rory Carroll 
 Saturday, 14 Nov 2026
 | 8:42 AM MYT
 share 
 bookmark 
 Tennis - WTA Finals Indian Wells - Indian Wells Tennis Garden, Indian Wells, California, U.S. - November 13, 2026 Ukraine's Elina Svitolina celebrates winning her group stage match against Belarus' Aryna Sabalenka REUTERS/Daniel Cole 
 INDIAN WELLS, ⁠California, Nov 13 (Reuters) - Elina Svitolina stunned Aryna Sabalenka 6-3 3-6 1-6 ⁠on Friday to reach the semifinals of the season-ending championships ‌in Indian Wells where she will face Linda Noskova.
 Svitolina redirected Sabalenka's power throughout the match, breaking the Belarusian's serve six times and pouncing on a short ball that she crushed ​on match point for her first win ⁠over Sabalenka in more than ⁠six years.
 Ukrainian Svitolina continued her long-standing policy of refusing post-match handshakes with players ⁠from ‌Russia and Belarus due to Russia's invasion of Ukraine, and did not shake Sabalenka's hand at the end of the match.
 The ⁠2018 WTA Finals champion Svitolina will next face ​Wimbledon champion Noskova on ‌Saturday for a spot in the final.
 It is a disappointing end ⁠to the ​season for Sabalenka, who won the "Sunshine Double" by winning both Indian Wells and the Miami Open earlier in the season, but did not win another title ⁠after that.
 She lost her world number one ranking ​to Elena Rybakina at the US Open and as the second seed was the favorite at the $10 million WTA Finals after Rybakina withdrew on the ⁠eve of the tournament due to illness.
 Earlier, tournament debutant Mirra Andreeva continued her dominant play, winning her third consecutive match in straight sets with a 6-2 6-1 dismantling of fellow Russian Diana Shnaider.
 Shnaider, Andreeva's friend and ​doubles partner, stepped in to replace Karolina Muchova, ⁠who withdrew from the last day of round-robin play at the tournament earlier ​on Friday with a gastrointestinal illness.
 Andreeva had ‌already booked her spot in the semi-finals ​prior to her match against Shnaider. She faces American Jessica Pegula in Saturday's semis.
 (Reporting by Rory Carroll; Editing by Stephen Coates)
